title: Midway Network: Learning Representations for Recognition and Motion from Latent Dynamics
claim: Prior self-supervised methods ignore motion or need an external motion predictor; ours infers motion latents internally from natural videos.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right progression, green dashed box highlights ours
description: Three side-by-side panels show the progression of self-supervised learning. Panel (a), traditional SSL, takes one dog image, makes two augmented crops, and sends each through an encoder trapezoid to a latent z1 or z2. The two are compared with a squared L2 loss. Panel (b), dense SSL on natural videos, takes road-scene frames x_t and x_{t+1}. An external optical-flow predictor, shown as a flow image, and a transform T warp z_t into a predicted z̃_t. The loss compares z̃_t with z_{t+1}. Panel (c), the proposed Midway Network, is outlined in a green dashed box. It uses a similar encoder path, but motion latents, drawn as purple squares, are inferred between z_t and z_{t+1}. These latents drive the prediction z̃_t, which feeds the same L2 loss. Real photos, black arrows and math labels are used throughout.
caption: \looseness=-10000 (a) Traditional SSL methods focus on learning representations for object recognition and lean on curated, iconic image data for training. (b) Dense SSL methods extend training to natural videos, but either do not utilize motion transformations [ref] for training or rely on external networks to incorporate motion [ref]. (c) Our proposed \model{} jointly learns representations of semantics and motion from solely natural videos via latent dynamics modeling. The learned image-level representations can be used towards downstream object recognition and motion understanding tasks.
abstract: Object recognition and motion understanding are key components of perception that complement each other. While self-supervised learning methods have shown promise in their ability to learn from unlabeled data, they have primarily focused on obtaining rich representations for either recognition or motion rather than both in tandem. On the other hand, latent dynamics modeling has been used in decision making to learn latent representations of observations and their transformations over time for control and planning tasks. In this work, we present Midway Network, a new self-supervised learning architecture that is the first to learn strong visual representations for both object recognition and motion understanding solely from natural videos, by extending latent dynamics modeling to this domain. Midway Network leverages a midway top-down path to infer motion latents between video frames, as well as a dense forward prediction objective and hierarchical structure to tackle the complex, multi-object scenes of natural videos. We demonstrate that after pretraining on two large-scale natural video datasets, Midway Network achieves strong performance on both semantic segmentation and optical flow tasks relative to prior self-supervised learning methods. We also show that Midway Network's learned dynamics can capture high-level correspondence via a novel analysis method based on forward feature perturbation.
